heard: A single teaspoon of a neutron star weighs one billion tons. Neutron stars are the gravitationally collapsed cores of massive stars formed following a supernova explosion. In 1967, graduate student Jocelyn Bell-Burnell detected a radio pulse so rhythmic she nicknamed it little green men. These stellar remnants pack the mass of a sun into a sphere only 12 miles wide. The extreme objects rotate hundreds of times per second and generate magnetic fields trillions of times stronger than Earth's. In 2017, scientists finally heard two of them collide through gravitational waves. These cosmic impacts created the heavy gold and platinum found in our jewelry today, leaving behind a single teaspoon of material that weighs one billion tons.
